newsitem.title: RUSSIA: RUSSIA UNEXIMBANK SAYS NORILSK DEAL ALMOST READY.
newsitem.headline: RUSSIA UNEXIMBANK SAYS NORILSK DEAL ALMOST READY.

text.p: The winners of a controversial tender for a controlling stake in Russian metals producer Norilsk Nickel said on Friday the deal was about to be signed.
ZAO Svift, which represented powerful Uneximbank's interests with a winning $250 million bid, would sign a sale agreement with the the federal property fund by Monday, an Uneximbank spokesman said.
Sergei Chernitsyn said the commission which ran the Norilsk auction would sign a final protocol on Friday signalling the formal end of the tender.

"In accordance with the law, the sale agreement should be signed within three calendar days from the signing of the final tender protocol by the tender commission," he said, adding it was unlikely to be signed at the weekend.

The results of the auction have hung in the balance since Tuesday, when a probe was ordered by senior government officials including Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin, dissatisfied with the way the the auction was run.
Chernomyrdin called for the sale to be halted on Tuesday, hours before the results were to be released, but at the last minute allowed it to proceed.

The shares had been held by Uneximbank under the state's so-called "shares for loans" programme which saw management control of some of the country's plum companies signed over to powerful banks in return for credits.
Norilsk is one of the world's top suppliers of platinum group metals and nickel.
